title: Cross-Dialect Generalization Without Retraining: Benchmarks and Evaluation of Schema-Derived Constrained Decoding for MLIR
abstract: arXiv:2607.18254v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Multi-Level Intermediate Representation (MLIR) underlies modern ML compiler infrastructure (TensorFlow, JAX/StableHLO, PyTorch Inductor, IREE), yet appears only in trace amounts in code-LM pretraining corpora. MLIR is also extensible by design: new dialects ship per application domain, so a fine-tuned model per dialect does not scale. We ask whether inference-time priors derived mechanically from each dialect's Operation Definition Specification (ODS) can substitute for gradient-based adaptation. First, we release four natural-language-to-MLIR benchmarks across three dialects (MLIR-Spec-150, Linalg-Spec-30, StableHLO-Spec-30, StableHLO-Held-Out-200), totaling 410 in-scope NL-to-MLIR pairs, plus a 25-program out-of-grammar stress set, with functional references on 30 Spec prompts, under Apache-2.0 with Gebru datasheets and Croissant 1.1 metadata. Second, we build a three-layer schema-derived constraint stack: a CFG over op signatures

translated_title: 无需重新训练的跨方言泛化：面向 MLIR 的模式派生约束解码基准与评估
translated_abstract: 多层中间表示（MLIR）是现代机器学习编译器基础设施（TensorFlow、JAX/StableHLO、PyTorch Inductor、IREE）的基础，然而在代码语言模型的预训练语料库中仅以极微量出现。此外，MLIR 在设计上具有可扩展性：每个应用领域都会发布新的方言，因此针对每个方言分别微调模型的做法无法规模化。我们探究能否从每个方言的操作定义规范（ODS）中机械地推导出推理时先验知识，以替代基于梯度的适配。首先，我们发布了涵盖三种方言的四个自然语言到 MLIR 的基准测试（MLIR-Spec-150、Linalg-Spec-30、StableHLO-Spec-30、StableHLO-Held-Out-200），共包含 410 个范围内的自然语言到 MLIR 配对样本，外加一个包含 25 个程序的语法外压力测试集，其中 30 个 Spec 提示词附有功能性参考实现，全部以 Apache-2.0 许可证发布，并附有 Gebru 数据表和 Croissant 1.1 元数据。其次，我们构建了一个三层的模式派生约束栈：基于操作签名的上下文无关文法（CFG）……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出从 MLIR 方言的操作定义规范（ODS）机械派生的推理时约束解码方法，无需重新训练即可实现跨方言泛化，并发布了涵盖三种方言共 410 个样本的四个自然语言到 MLIR 基准测试数据集。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes inference-time constrained decoding mechanically derived from each MLIR dialect's Operation Definition Specification (ODS), enabling cross-dialect generalization without retraining, and releases four NL-to-MLIR benchmarks totaling 410 samples across three dialects.
